intro: Your hands touch hundreds of things every day. A door. A crayon. A dog. A sandwich. Tiny germs ride along on your hands. You cannot see them. But they can make you sick.
In this unit you will find out where germs hide and how they travel. You will learn when to wash. You will learn the five steps and how to count twenty seconds without a clock.
By the end you will be able to wash your hands the right way all by yourself. You will know what to do when there is no sink. And you will know how to keep germs to yourself with an elbow.
bigQuestion: How do clean hands keep me and my friends healthy?

timeline.t: Brush your teeth for two minutes before breakfast.
Wash before you eat, then sit down.
Wash every time, even when you are in a hurry.
Come inside, go to the sink, then do anything else.
Wet, lather, scrub for two songs, rinse, dry.
Sneeze into your elbow, toss the tissue, wash.
Feed the pet, then wash your hands.
No sink? Rub sanitizer until dry with a grown-up.
Wash before you help, and wash before you eat.
Brush your teeth again and stand the brush up to dry.

test.q: Why can you not see germs?
choices: They are invisible only at night
test.why: Germs are so tiny that a microscope is needed to see them.

test.q: How do germs mostly travel from a toy to your mouth?
test.why: Hands touch things and then touch the face, carrying germs along.

test.q: Which is a time you must wash?
test.why: Germs on hands go onto food, so wash before every meal and snack.

test.q: You just petted a cat. What next?
test.why: Animal fur carries germs, so wash after touching any pet.

test.q: What do the five steps start with?
test.why: Wet, lather, scrub, rinse, dry is the order.
Twenty seconds, about two rounds of the birthday song, is the standard.
Soap lifts germs and dirt so running water can carry them away.
The elbow does not touch shared things, so germs stay put.

test.q: Kim dries her clean hands on a towel used all week. What happens?
choices: Germs go back on her hands
test.why: A dirty towel puts germs right back; use a clean one.

test.q: There is no sink on the bus. What can you use before a snack?
test.why: Sanitizer is the backup when there is no sink; rub it in until dry.

write.prompt: Draw and write the five steps of washing your hands in order. Next to each step, tell why it is there. Then write one time in your day when you must wash.
tips: Put the steps in order: wet, lather, scrub, rinse, dry.
Say how long the scrub step takes and how you count it.
Name the parts of your hands you must not forget.
Tell what you dry with and why it must be clean.
